'''Randy Foye''' (born September 24, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played collegiately at [[Villanova University]]. He was selected seventh overall in the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]], but was immediately traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], and later traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] where he began his career.<ref name="draft">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/Trail_Blazers_Land_Brandon_Roy-183312-1177.html|title=TRAIL BLAZERS LAND BRANDON ROY AND LAMARCUS ALDRIDGE|work=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2006|access-date=February 27, 2016}}</ref>

==High school career==
Foye attended [[East Side High School (Newark, New Jersey)|East Side High School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey|Newark]], where he was selected as New Jersey Player of the Year, before being recruited by [[Jay Wright (coach)|Jay Wright]] and Villanova.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/home/playerfile/randy_foye/career_stats.html|title=Randy Foye: Career Stats and Totals|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 21, 2006}}</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Scout.com]], Foye was listed as the No. 7 shooting guard and the No. 37 player in the nation in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/player/10504n-randy-foye|title=Randy Foye Recruiting Profile|work=Scout.com|access-date=March 21, 2006}}</ref>

==College career==
Foye, along with [[Allan Ray]], [[Curtis Sumpter]], and Jason Fraser were proclaimed as the players to lead the Villanova Wildcats back to a championship. Foye and Ray reached the [[Elite Eight]] of the [[2006 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2006 NCAA Tournament]], playing with the other three starters in the four-guard offense ([[Kyle Lowry]], [[Mike Nardi]] and [[Will Sheridan]]), while Sumpter was sidelined as a medical redshirt with a knee injury.

Foye's college career was productive and eventful, but his [[2005–06 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|senior season]] was by far the best statistically.

In the [[2005 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2005 NCAA Tournament]], Foye averaged 20 points in three games, before a heartbreaking loss to #1 seed and eventual national champion [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|North Carolina]] in which Foye scored a career-high 28 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=254000022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090108052644/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=254000022|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 8, 2009|title=Villanova's spirited surge in closing minutes falls short|publisher=ESPN|date=March 26, 2005|access-date=March 21, 2006}}</ref> He was named third-team all Big East that year.

In 2006, Foye won the honor of [[Big East Player of the Year]], beating out teammate [[Allan Ray]], [[University of Connecticut|Connecticut]] star [[Rudy Gay]] and the league's leading scorer [[Quincy Douby]] of [[Rutgers University|Rutgers]].

Villanova tied for the Big East regular season championship with Uconn and split their two games with the Huskies, winning the one played at home, in what some called the biggest Villanova win in over 20 years. Their final Big East regular season record was 14–2 in what some called the toughest conference ever.{{Citation needed|date=June 2007}} Overall, their record was 28–5. In the NCAA Tournament in 2006, Foye continued to be Villanova's biggest scoring threat. He had 24 points in their second-round game against [[University of Arizona|Arizona]] in a winning effort. Foye scored a team-high 25 points in his final game as a Wildcat, on March 26, 2006, a 75–62 loss to [[University of Florida|Florida]] in the Elite Eight.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=264000046|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120719203057/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=264000046|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 19, 2012|title=Noah's monster night sends Florida to Final Four|publisher=ESPN|date=March 26, 2006|access-date=March 26, 2006}}</ref>

As a senior Foye averaged 20.5 points, 5.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.4 steals, and 0.6 blocks, with a field goal percentage of 41.1%.

==Professional career==

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2006–2009)===
On June 28, 2006, Foye was selected seventh overall in the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]], but was immediately traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], and later traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref name="draft" /> He entered his rookie year on a team that already had six guards on its roster. Off-season free-agent acquisition [[Mike James (basketball, born 1975)|Mike James]] was slated to start at [[point guard]], Foye's most likely position in the NBA, with [[Ricky Davis]] at small forward and [[Rashad McCants]] at shooting guard. This left Foye to battle for minutes on a bench full of guards. In November, Foye's first month as a professional basketball player, Timberwolves coach [[Dwane Casey]] only gave Foye an average of 14.6 minutes per game. Foye, however, was productive whenever he was given minutes. He scored in double digits in each of the four games he was given 20 or more minutes of playing time.
[[Image:Randy Foye Wiz.jpg|thumb|160px|Foye as a member of the [[Washington Wizards]]]]

In December 2007, Foye's minutes per game average increased to 19.6 and he scored in double digits in half of the T-Wolves' games. However, after Dwane Casey's firing after the Twolves' 40th game (when they had a record of 20–20), the Twolves struggled, yet the young star played well when given minutes. In March, Foye saw nearly 24 minutes of playing time a night, and in April saw almost 27 minutes a night to perform.

Foye played all 82 games (12 starts) in his rookie season and averaged 22.9 minutes, 10.1 points, 2.7 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 0.65 steals, and 0.3 blocks per game. Among rookies, he ranked fifth in scoring (10.1 ppg), eighth in field goal percentage (43.4%), third in 3-point shooting percentage (37%), third in free throw shooting percentage (85%), 5th in assists (2.8 apg) and 9th in steals (0.65 spg).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/f/foyera01/gamelog/2007/|title=Randy Foye 2006-07 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 27, 2016}}</ref> He was one of the most consistent rookie performers and was selected to the NBA All-Rookie First Team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/news/allrookie_070508.html|title=Roy Headlines 2006-07 NBA T-Mobile All-Rookie Team|work=NBA.com|date=May 11, 2007|access-date=February 27, 2016}}</ref>

On December 23, 2008, Foye pulled down 16 rebounds to set a career high and break the team record of 15 for a guard set by [[Isaiah Rider]] in 1996. Foye also had 26 points and 1 assist in the 99–93 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=281223024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090106091221/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=281223024|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 6, 2009|title=Parker, Spurs send Wolves to 13th straight loss|publisher=ESPN|date=December 24, 2008|access-date=February 27, 2016}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2009–2010)===
On June 23, 2009, Foye, along with [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)|Mike Miller]], was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] for [[Oleksiy Pecherov]], [[Etan Thomas]], [[Darius Songaila]], and a first round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4282279|title=Source: Foye, Miller head to Wiz|publisher=ESPN|date=June 24, 2009|access-date=October 2, 2010}}</ref>

On January 9, 2010, Foye was fined $10,000 by the Washington Wizards for participating in [[Gilbert Arenas]]' antics before a game on January 5, 2010, against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Arenas was being investigated for a prior incident involving guns in the Wizards' locker room, but made light of the accusations by pointing his finger at his teammates, as if he were shooting them. His teammates were photographed smiling and laughing with him.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4810297|title=Wiz fine Blatche, McGee, Foye, Young|publisher=ESPN|date=January 9, 2010|access-date=January 9, 2010}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2010–2012)===
[[File:Randy Foye Clippers.jpg|thumb|right|Foye (center) with [[DeAndre Jordan]] (left) and [[Nick Young (basketball)|Nick Young]] (right) in 2011]]
On July 8, 2010, Foye was signed by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews_100708.html|title=CLIPPERS SIGN FREE AGENT GUARD RANDY FOYE|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2010|access-date=July 9, 2010}}</ref> Foye started the year as a backup, but moved into the starting rotation following an injury to [[Eric Gordon]] and trade of [[Baron Davis]]. On February 11, 2011, he scored 32 points with seven assists and two steals while shooting 50 percent from the field in a 99–92 loss to the [[2010–11 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/310226012|title=Celtics 99-92 Clippers (Feb 26, 2011) Final Score|work=ESPN.com|date=February 22, 2011|access-date=June 19, 2011}}</ref>

In his first season in LA, Foye developed chemistry with [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|Rookie of the Year]] [[Blake Griffin]], establishing himself as LA's shooting guard heading into the 2011–12 season. However a busy [[2011 NBA lockout|lockout]]-delayed offseason saw the Clippers acquire All-Stars [[Chris Paul]] and [[Chauncey Billups]], moving Foye back to a reserve role. He would end up starting most off the year and all 11 playoff games after Billups sustained a season-ending injury, averaging 11 points, two rebounds and two assists a game.

===Utah Jazz (2012–2013)===
On July 25, 2012, Foye agreed to terms with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-agrees-terms-guard-randy-foye|title=Jazz Agrees to Terms with Guard Randy Foye|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 25, 2012|access-date=July 25, 2012}}</ref> During the one season Foye played for the Jazz, he set the franchise record for most 3-pointers made in a year, making 178 out of 434 shots (with a shooting percentage of 41%).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/f/foyera01/gamelog/2013/|title=Randy Foye 2012-13 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 27, 2016}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2013–2016)===
On July 10, 2013, Foye was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] as part of a three-team trade involving the Jazz and the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-acquire-randy-foye-three-team-trade|title=Denver Nuggets Acquire Randy Foye In Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 10, 2013|access-date=July 14, 2013}}</ref> On February 3, 2014, Foye hit the first game-winning shot of his eight-year NBA career, making a 30-foot three-pointer as time expired to claim a 116–115 win over the Los Angeles Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140203/LACDEN/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Nuggets 116, Clippers 115|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 3, 2014|access-date=April 9, 2016}}</ref>

On December 23, 2015, Foye scored a season-high 31 points and made seven three-pointers in a 104–96 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151223/DENPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Foye scores 31 points, Nuggets bounce back to beat Suns|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 23, 2015|access-date=December 23, 2015}}</ref> Statistical lineup analysis from the 2015–16 season showed that several of Denver’s most effective units in net rating featured Foye and rookie [[Nikola Jokić]] playing together.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thednvr.com/nikola-jokic-randy-foye-could-be-key-to-unlocking-denver-nuggets-lopsided-lineups/|title=Nikola Jokic, Randy Foye could be key to unlocking Denver Nuggets lopsided lineups|work=DNVR Sports|publisher=Kalen Deremo|date=November 10, 2015|access-date=December 23, 2015}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2016)===
On February 18, 2016, Foye was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for [[D. J. Augustin]], [[Steve Novak]], two second-round draft picks and cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/pressrelease_foye_160218|title=Thunder Acquires Randy Foye|work=NBA.com|date=February 18, 2016|access-date=February 18, 2016}}</ref> Three days later, he made his debut for the Thunder in a 115–92 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], recording two points and one assist in 14 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160221/CLEOKC/gameinfo.html|title=Love scores 29, leads Cavaliers past Thunder 115-92|work=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2016|access-date=February 27, 2016}}</ref> Foye appeared in the first conference finals series of his career that postseason, as the Thunder lost to the defending NBA champion [[Golden State Warriors]] in seven games in the Western Conference Finals.

===Brooklyn Nets (2016–2017)===
On July 15, 2016, Foye signed with his hometown team the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/07/15/brooklyn-nets-sign-randy-foye|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Randy Foye|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}}</ref> He missed the first six games of the 2016–17 season with a strained right hamstring.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899551|title=Nets keep Wolves winless on the road with 119-110 win|work=ESPN.com|date=November 8, 2016|access-date=November 9, 2016}}</ref> On December 26, 2016, Foye made a three-pointer to beat the buzzer and give the Nets a 120–118 victory over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899905|title=Randy Foye's 3 gives Nets 120-118 victory over Hornets|work=ESPN.com|date=December 26, 2016|access-date=December 27, 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Foye was born with a condition called [[situs inversus]] that caused him to be born with his organs reversed, meaning his heart is on the right side of his body and his liver is on the left.<ref>{{cite web|last=Mascaro|first=Chris|url=https://www.si.com/si-wire/2013/10/04/randy-foyes-heart-is-in-the-wrong-place|title=Nuggets guard Randy Foye's heart is in the wrong place -- literally|work=SI.com|date=October 4, 2013|access-date=December 23, 2015}}</ref> Due to his inverted organs, Foye featured on a 2015 BBC series called Countdown to Life explaining how his condition was caused. The show stated Foye was lucky to be alive, because his organs are a perfect mirror image of the normal system of human organs. If only a few of his organs had swapped, this could have caused severe disability or death.<ref>{{cite web|last=Mount|first=Harry|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/tvandradio/tv-and-radio-reviews/11865063/Countdown-to-Life-the-Extraordinary-Making-of-You-review.html|title=Countdown to Life: the Extraordinary Making of You, review: 'gripping'|work=Telegraph.co.uk|date=September 14, 2015|access-date=September 14, 2015}}</ref>

Foye has also appeared on a PBS documentary ''[[9 Months That Made You]]'' which premiered June 29, 2016 discussing his condition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pbs.org/program/nine-months-that-made-you/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160626110039/http://www.pbs.org/program/nine-months-that-made-you/|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 26, 2016|title=9 Months That Made You|work=PBS|date=June 29, 2016|access-date=July 4, 2017}}</ref>

Foye appeared in the sitcom ''[[Wingin' It]]'', guest-starring as himself.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bsqvFT5h3WQ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211222/bsqvFT5h3WQ |archive-date=2021-12-22 |url-status=live|title=Wingin' It with Foye|work=YouTube.com|date=May 24, 2010|access-date=September 14, 2015}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

A resident of [[Rumson, New Jersey]], Foye purchased his home from [[Bruce Springsteen]].<ref>Hyman, Vicki. [http://realestate.nj.com/realestate-news/2016/05/bruce_springsteen_rumson_home.html "Bruce Springsteen selling Rumson home to NBA's Randy Foye for $1.7M"], NJ Advance Media for [[NJ.com]], May 11, 2016. Accessed February 28, 2018. "Bruce Springsteen has sold off one of his Rumson homes to Newark native and NBA player Randy Foye for $1.737 million, according to Monmouth County records and Zillow.com."</ref>

Foye has two daughters, Paige Christine Foye and Penny Carter Foye.<ref name="bioN">{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/resources/static/team/v2/jazz/2012-13-Jazz-MediaGuide.pdf|title=Randy Foye Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 23, 2015}}</ref>

Started the Randy Foye Foundation in 2007 which focuses on helping inner city kids in [[Newark, NJ]].<ref name="bioN" />
